#The Vault helper protocol

Wren talks to its Vault helper, wren-vault, through two anonymous pipes: the helper's standard input carries the requests, its standard output the answers. The design is in bitwarden.md. The helper is a separate program under GPL-3.0-only, in its own repository; its README.md has the same description. This page and that README must stay equal: a change of the protocol changes both, and PROTOCOL_VERSION in src/vault/protocol.odin and in the helper.

The protocol is generic: accounts, items (logins, cards, identities) and plain values. No type of the Bitwarden SDK crosses the pipe.

Version 5 (helper 0.5.0). Changes from version 4: new requests save (create a login, or update one) and generate (a password or a passphrase, by the SDK's generator; the vault need not be unlocked); rows of search carry kind (login, card or identity; secure notes and SSH keys are not listed), rows of logins_for carry kind login; fill takes the fields of cards and identities; the error save_failed; search is paged: it takes offset, limit (0: 100, at most 500) and kinds, answers total, and an empty query lists every item of the asked kinds; new requests passkeys_for and passkey_assert (the vault's passkeys answer a page's navigator.credentials.get) and the error assert_failed.

Version 4 (helper 0.4.0). Changes from version 3: new requests password_hint, device_request, device_poll, passkey_options and login_passkey; login takes remember; unlock takes prf and credential_id; hello answers passkey; the errors denied, expired, no_passkey and account_locked. Every token request carries the headers Auth-Email (a password login) and Bitwarden-Client-Version, without which the server refuses it.

Version 3 (helper 0.3.0). Changes from version 2: new requests search and totp; fill takes the field totp; logins_for applies the rules StartsWith and Exact and the account's equivalent domains, its rows carry the match types equivalent, starts_with and exact, and its answer carries equivalent; the error no_totp.

Version 2 (helper 0.2.0) changed from version 1: the server choice is Wren's (the helper gets URLs as before); login carries code and provider instead of totp, and answers need_device_code; new requests login_api_key, logout, pin_set, pin_clear; unlock takes pin; hello takes idle_seconds and answers login and pin; the event locked.

#Frames

  • Each message is one frame: a 4-byte unsigned length, little-endian, then that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one object).
  • The length is from 1 to 1 048 576 (1 MiB). A frame outside these bounds ends the connection.
  • The helper answers each request, in the order of the requests. keepalive has no answer.
  • The helper writes nothing else on its standard output, and no value of the vault on its standard error.
  • The helper exits when its standard input closes, after it answers lock or logout, and at its idle deadline.

#Requests and answers

A request is {"id": <integer from 1>, "op": "<name>", ...fields}. The answer repeats the id:

  • success: {"id": n, "ok": true, ...fields}
  • failure: {"id": n, "ok": false, "error": "<code>", "message": "<sentence>"}

An event answers no request: {"id": 0, "ok": true, "event": "<name>"}.

#Login steps

  • provider is authenticator (an authenticator app's code; the default), email (a code by email) or device (the code of the server's new-device mail). providers lists the second steps of the account that the helper supports (authenticator, email); an account with none of them gets unsupported_two_factor.
  • A login with a second step is two requests or more. The first login (email and password) answers need_two_factor or need_device_code; the helper keeps the email, the password and the device identifier of that login. The second login carries the same email, the code and its provider: Wren sends the master password once. A failed second step forgets the kept password.
  • resend asks for a code again. With provider email, the helper asks the server to mail the two-step code and answers need_two_factor with email_sent true. With device, it sends the first step again and the server mails a new code. email_sent is also true when the email code is the account's only second step: the server mailed it.

#Item kinds

  • A card row: name the item's name, username the brand and the last 4 digits (Visa *1234, "" when no number), uri "".
  • An identity row: name the item's name, username the full name or else the email, uri "".
  • has_totp is false for cards and identities. A row without kind is a login (version 4); Wren drops a row of a kind it does not know.

#Fill fields

  • A login: username, password, totp.
  • A card: cardholder, number, exp_month (as stored, 1 to 12), exp_year (4 digits when stored so), code, brand.
  • An identity: title, first_name, middle_name, last_name, full_name (first, middle and last, single spaces), address1, address2, address3, city, state, postal_code, country, company, email, phone, username, ssn, passport, license.
  • A field of another kind of item gives nothing for it, and no error. no_item: an id that is neither a login, a card nor an identity.

#Search

  • Each word of query must be in the item's name, its user name (a card's brand and last digits, an identity's name or email) or one of its URIs. An empty query matches every item of the asked kinds.
  • The answer is one page: the matches sorted by name, from offset, at most limit. total counts every match, so that Wren asks the next page (offset = the rows it holds) only while there are more.

#Save

  • On an update, only the given non-empty fields change (username, password); the item keeps its password history as the SDK does it. The uri is added to the item's URIs when none matches it.
  • The helper encrypts with the SDK, sends it to the server (POST /api/ciphers for a creation, PUT /api/ciphers/{id} for an update) and puts the result into its local copy of the vault: logins_for, search and fill see it at once, without a sync.
  • Errors: locked, no_item (an update of an id that is not a login), save_failed (the server refused it or cannot be reached; the message says why).

#Passkeys of sites

  • passkeys_for lists the vault's passkeys (the passkeys of login items) whose relying party is rp_id (ASCII case aside). With a non-empty allow (the credential ids of the page's allowCredentials, base64url), it lists only the passkeys in it. A passkey without a user handle is not listed. username is the passkey's user name, else its display name, else the login's username, else the item's name. credential_id and user_handle are base64url. The rows are sorted by item name.
  • passkey_assert signs with the SDK's authenticator (bitwarden-fido). The authenticator data holds the SHA-256 of rp_id, the flags UP and UV (an unlocked vault is a verified user) and the sign count. The signature (ES256, DER) is over the authenticator data and client_data_hash. Wren makes the clientDataJSON and its hash: the helper sees only the hash.
  • A passkey with a sign counter (not 0) gets its new count saved in its item, as save does (PUT {api}/ciphers/{id}). A failed save does not fail the assertion.
  • Errors: locked; bad_request (an empty rp_id, a client_data_hash that is not 32 bytes); no_item (the item or the passkey is not in the vault, or not of rp_id); assert_failed (the authenticator refused to sign).

#Idle deadline

hello's idle_seconds (0: none) is the helper's own lock. When no request (keepalive included) comes for that long, the helper writes the event locked and exits. Wren sends it its own idle time and a margin (vault.lock.idle_minutes × 60 + 120); Wren locks first, on its own timer, and sends a keepalive at most once a minute while the user is active.

#Errors

bad_request, bad_protocol, no_hello, bad_server, bad_credentials, unsupported_two_factor, unsupported_account, network, login_failed, no_account, bad_password, bad_pin, pin_reset, no_pin, no_state, denied, expired, no_passkey, account_locked, locked, sync_failed, session_expired, no_item, no_totp, save_failed, assert_failed, decrypt, state_write, state_format. The helper's README says what each means.

#The helper's identity at the server

The helper sends its own token request (the SDK's sends the device type ChromeBrowser and one device identifier for every SDK user, and cannot carry the new-device code): client id web, device type 14 (UnknownBrowser), device name Wren, and a random device identifier made at the first login and kept in the state. The SDK's HTTP client gets the same device type (the Device-Type header). A renewal with an API key goes through the SDK and still names its fixed device; no new-device check applies to API keys.

#Matching

The helper selects the logins whose saved URI matches the page: Domain (the URI's host is the page's registrable domain or a subdomain of it: domain; or one of the domains the account makes equivalent to it, or a subdomain of one: equivalent; a page without a registrable domain uses Host), Host (same host and port), StartsWith (the page's address starts with the URI) and Exact (the page's address is the URI), both addresses as the URL standard serializes them. RegularExpression and Never match nothing. An item saved for https never matches an http page. The equivalent domains are the account's own groups and the server's global groups it did not exclude, from the last sync.

Wren checks every returned row again with its own Public Suffix List (src/vault/match.odin) on the blocking pool, before a surface shows it. An equivalent row stays only if the saved host's registrable domain is in the answer's equivalent. A row with a match type Wren does not know is dropped when the answer is read. A row that fails the check is zeroed and dropped. search rows are not checked: a login of them fills only when the same item is also a checked row of the focused document (docs/bitwarden.md 3.5, rule 10). Cards and identities have no site: they fill only into the card or address fields where the user picked them (docs/bitwarden.md 4.10).

#Wren's side

src/vault (no interface, no dependency on the browser):

FileWhat
protocol.odinThe requests, written into one buffer reserved large enough at once; the answers, decoded into owned values. Every string that can hold a value is zeroed before it is freed.
transport.odin, process.odinThe helper as a child process: a reader thread starts it, reads and decodes frames and posts each answer to the loop; a writer thread writes the queued frames in order and zeroes each. The loop thread never blocks on the helper.
vault.odinThe one state of the Vault, the requests and their deadlines (vault.request.timeout_ms), the four sets of rows (the tab's document, the focused frame's document, the search, the cards or identities of a card or address field; the last two page by page), the fill's ticket, the copies, the save offer and its never-save list, the generated value, a page's passkey requests (each answered once to its caller's callback: the rows or the signature, a refusal, timeout or locked), the idle and sync timers, the blocking jobs (locating the helper, the account and never-save files, the check of the rows, the join of an ended helper).
match.odinWren's match check.
settings.odinThe vault.* preferences and the server addresses (US, EU, self-hosted).
